samples.summary: Page Setup dialog and `assertUsablePageSetup` use different boundaries; an accepted form can throw an uncaught RangeError out of the submit handler
samples.evidence: The dialog rejects only `left+right >= pageWidth` (line 145) / `top+bottom >= pageHeight` (line 147), while `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1013) rejects `margins.left + margins.right > width - MIN_CONTENT_PX` (i.e. > width-1). Any sum in the half-open band `(width-1, width)` passes the dialog and is refused by the editor. `handleSubmit` calls `editor.setPageSetup(...)` with no try/catch, so the RangeError escapes a React event handler: the dialog stays open, nothing is applied, and the user gets no feedback. Reachable whenever the effective page width/height is not an integer (a stored paperSize that did not come from a preset or from the twips→px rounding in the DOCX parser), since the dialog rounds margins to whole px but the page dimension is not rounded.

samples.summary: `URI_CHARS` allowlist silently drops legitimate links/images whose URLs contain characters outside RFC 3986 (`|`, `{`, `}`, `^`, `"`, backtick) or an `&name;`-shaped substring
samples.evidence: `isLiteralDestination` requires the whole destination to match `URI_CHARS` and to contain no `ENTITY_REFERENCE`. Real-world URLs routinely carry unencoded `|`, `{`/`}` (templated/tracking links), and a query such as `?a=1§x=2` matches `ENTITY_REFERENCE` (`§`). In those cases `inlineToMarkdown` silently drops the link (only the bare text survives) and `imageInline` degrades the picture to the literal `[image]`. That is data loss in the exported `.md` for inputs that are neither hostile nor malformed, and there is no diagnostic anywhere.

samples.summary: Routing `parsePageSetup` through `resolvePageSetup` can silently rescale the margins of an imported landscape .docx, because the fit is measured against the swapped (portrait) box
samples.evidence: `parsePageSetup` stores the raw `<w:pgSz w:w>`/`w:h` (which Word already writes swapped for landscape) into `paperSize.width/height` and sets `orientation='landscape'`. `resolvePageSetup` then measures the margin fit against `getEffectiveDimensions`-style swapped values (types.ts:841-843), i.e. against the *narrow* dimension for a landscape document. A landscape file whose left+right margins exceed the short edge (but fit the real page) now has both margins proportionally shrunk by `fitMargins` on import — a silent geometry change that the previous raw parse did not make. The underlying double-swap is pre-existing, but the new clamp turns it into a data rewrite.

samples.summary: Format painter's table-cell branch can read from an empty block at `offset: 1`, resolving to an unrelated/empty style
samples.evidence: `formatSourcePosition` falls back to `cell?.blocks[0]` when no cell block has text, then returns `{ blockId: first.id, offset: 1 }`. For an empty block, offset 1 is past every run, so `caretInlineStyle` (model/caret-style.ts:64) falls through to the block's last run or `{}` — the painter then picks up an empty format and, because `captureFormatAtCursor` bakes every boolean to `false`, a subsequent paste actively *clears* bold/italic/etc. on the target instead of no-opping.

samples.summary: Ruler margin drag can now throw a RangeError from inside a pointer event handler
samples.evidence: `ruler.onMarginChange` now routes through `writePageSetup`, which calls `assertUsablePageSetup` and throws. The ruler's own guard (view/ruler/index.ts:408-410) is measured against `cachedPageWidth`/`cachedPageHeight` captured at the last `render()`; if the page geometry changed underneath (a collaborator's CRDT page-setup write between render and drag-apply, or a first drag before a re-render), the drag can produce margins the assert refuses, and the throw propagates out of the ruler's pointermove/pointerup listener with no catch anywhere on that path. Previously this path could not throw.

samples.summary: `parseInches` rejects a trailing-dot intermediate value, so the error banner and disabled Apply flash while the user types "1.5"
samples.evidence: `/^\d*\.?\d+$/` requires at least one digit after the dot, so the transient value "1." produces `null` and the component renders "Margins must be zero or a positive number of inches." mid-typing. The comment justifying the regex only discusses `""` and `"0x60"`.

samples.summary: `copiedFormatListeners` are never cleared on editor teardown
samples.evidence: `onCopiedFormatChange` pushes into `copiedFormatListeners` and only the returned unsubscribe removes entries; no `dispose()`/destroy path clears the array. A `TextEditor` disposed while a subscriber is still registered keeps the callback (and whatever it closes over) alive through the notifier.
